title: Accounts Assistant
description:
You're the person who spots when an invoice doesn't look right - and wants to find out why.

If that sounds familiar, I'm recruiting for a growing business where that approach will be valued.

This is a role for someone who enjoys sales and purchase ledger work and takes pride in getting the detail right. You'll get to understand what the business delivers, work closely with colleagues across the team and make sure the paperwork reflects what's actually happened.

There's plenty to keep you interested. Different customers have different billing requirements, so you'll need to stay organised, ask questions and investigate anything that doesn't add up.

What you'll be doing

The role is mainly sales ledger, alongside purchase ledger responsibilities and some support with customer payments. You'll be:
- Preparing and checking sales invoices against supporting information.
- Making sure customers receive the documents they need, in the format they require.
- Working with operational colleagues to resolve missing information and billing queries.
- Processing supplier invoices and investigating discrepancies.
- Supporting supplier statement reconciliations and keeping ledger records accurate.
- Helping with payment queries and credit control cover when needed.

Who I'd like to speak to

You'll have practical experience in sales ledger, purchase ledger or a broader accounts administration role, with a sound understanding of how the ledgers work.

Just as important is how you approach the job. You ask questions, follow things through and pay attention to what's happening around you. If something looks unusual, you check it before moving on.

You'll be comfortable with a busy workload, confident learning systems and happy speaking with colleagues, customers and suppliers to get an answer.

An accountancy qualification isn't essential. Relevant experience, accuracy and a willingness to learn the business will carry more weight.

Why consider it?

You'll join a close-knit team in a growing business where your contribution is easy to see. There's room to build your knowledge, put forward ideas and become someone colleagues trust to keep things running properly.

The position is focused on ledger work, so it should suit someone who enjoys that area of finance and wants to take real ownership of it.

If you'd like to hear more, please send your CV to Jason at Abbeygate Search or get in touch for an initial conversation.

Interim Accounts Payable Specialist - Backlog & Ledger Clean-UpNorthamptonshire £17-£19 per hour 40 hours per week Hybrid working Immediate start
Are you an experienced Accounts Payable professional who enjoys getting stuck into a challenge, resolving complex queries and bringing order to an overloaded purchase ledger?

We are working with a leading agile and forward-thinking organisation who are looking for an experienced Interim Accounts Payable Specialist to join their finance team on an immediate basis, with the assignment running until the end of April 2027.

This is very much a hands-on AP clean-up role, with a key focus on tackling an existing backlog, reviewing historic transactions, clearing aged items and resolving outstanding supplier queries.

You'll play an important role in getting the purchase ledger back up to date, ensuring outstanding issues are investigated and accounts are brought back into good order.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who thrives on making a tangible difference, is confident taking ownership of a busy ledger and has previous experience of successfully clearing AP backlogs.

The Role

Working as part of the finance team, you will take ownership of a range of outstanding Accounts Payable activities, with a particular emphasis on historic ledger clean-up and query resolution.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Working through a substantial backlog of outstanding supplier invoices and purchase ledger transactions.
- Reviewing and clearing aged items and historic balances on supplier accounts.
- Investigating discrepancies, unmatched invoices, payment issues and outstanding queries.
- Reconciling supplier statements and resolving long-standing differences.
- Proactively contacting suppliers and internal departments to obtain information and drive queries through to resolution.
- Identifying and correcting ledger issues to ensure supplier accounts are accurate and up to date.
- Prioritising outstanding work, managing competing demands and making measurable progress against the backlog.
- Providing general AP support as required to ensure the smooth running of the function.

About You

We're looking for someone who can hit the ground running and is comfortable rolling up their sleeves to get stuck into a busy and potentially untidy purchase ledger.

Ideally, you will have:
- Strong, demonstrable experience within Accounts Payable / Purchase Ledger.
- Previous experience of clearing significant AP backlogs or undertaking ledger clean-up projects.
- Confidence investigating historic transactions, aged balances and long-standing supplier queries.
- Strong supplier statement reconciliation and query resolution skills.
- A proactive, methodical approach, with the ability to investigate issues rather than simply process invoices.
- Excellent attention to detail and the ability to work through high volumes of outstanding work efficiently.
- The confidence to take ownership, use your initiative and make an immediate impact.
- Availability to start immediately and commit to the assignment through to April 2027.

What's on Offer?
- £17-£19 per hour (inc. Holiday uplift) depending on experience.
- 40-hour working week - 8:30am - 5:30pm
- Hybrid working - four days in the office and one day from home.
- Immediate start available.
- A long-term interim assignment through to the end of April 2027.
- The opportunity to make a real difference by helping a finance function get its AP ledger back on track.

Interested?
If you're an experienced Accounts Payable professional who knows their way around a purchase ledger, enjoys solving problems and has a proven ability to clear backlogs and get supplier accounts back into shape, we'd love to hear from you.

We're particularly keen to hear from candidates who are immediately available and can hit the ground running.

title: Finance Officer
description:
Finance Officer

Are you an experienced finance professional looking for a varied role within a growing and entrepreneurial business?

We are looking for an organised, proactive and detail-focused Finance Officer to join our finance team. This is a varied role covering the day-to-day financial operations of a portfolio of companies, with responsibility for maintaining accurate financial records, supporting month-end processes and providing reliable financial information to the wider business.

The ideal candidate will have previous experience in a finance or bookkeeping role and be comfortable working independently across a range of accounting activities. You may be part or fully qualified in a recognised accountancy qualification, or an experienced bookkeeper looking to take the next step in your career.

The Client

From our office in NN3 Moulton Park Industrial Estate We provide card processing services supporting businesses to take payments face-to-face at point of sale, online, over the phone and through vending.

Our services include the supply and support of point-of-sale credit and debit card processing machines to small businesses, retailers, charities, and vending machine operators.

The Role

Reporting directly to the Financial Controller, the Finance Officer will be responsible for the day-to-day accounting activities.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who has good practical accounting experience and is looking for a role where they can take ownership of their work, develop their skills, and become an important part of a small finance team.

You will work closely with the Financial Controller and other areas of the business to ensure that financial information is accurate, complete, and available on a timely basis.

Key ResponsibilitiesGeneral Accounting & Bookkeeping
- Maintaining accurate and up-to-date accounting records across a portfolio of Group companies.
- Processing and posting financial transactions accurately and within required timescales.
- Maintaining customer and supplier accounts and ensuring records are complete and accurate.
- Completing daily and monthly bank reconciliations and investigating any discrepancies.
- Processing purchase invoices, supplier payments, and remittances.
- Processing sales invoices and customer receipts.
- Managing direct debit collections and accurately matching payments to customer accounts.
- Liaising with customers and suppliers to resolve account queries and outstanding balances.
- Maintaining appropriate records and supporting documentation.

Month-End & Management Accounts
- Supporting the Financial Controller with the monthly management accounts process.
- Completing month-end reconciliations and ensuring balance sheet accounts are accurate and supported.
- Preparing and posting month-end journals, including accruals, prepayments, and depreciation.
- Assisting with the preparation of monthly management reports.
- Providing accurate financial information and analysis when required.
- Identifying and investigating unusual transactions, variances, or discrepancies.

Financial Administration & Support
- Providing information and support to other departments within the Group where required.
- Maintaining organised and accurate financial records.
- Assisting with the administration of the finance function and ensuring processes are followed consistently.
- Supporting the Financial Controller with ad-hoc financial analysis and projects.
- Identifying opportunities to improve finance processes, efficiency, and controls.

About You

We are looking for someone who is confident working across a broad range of finance activities and who takes pride in producing accurate and timely work.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience in a finance, accounts, or bookkeeping role.
- A good understanding of double-entry bookkeeping and core accounting principles.
- Experience of bank reconciliations, purchase and sales ledgers and general bookkeeping.
- Experience of month-end processes, including journals, accruals, and prepayments.
- Strong attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy.
- Good numerical and analytical skills and the ability to work with large volumes of financial data.
- Good Excel skills and confidence working with spreadsheets.
- Experience using cloud-based accounting software such as Xero, QuickBooks, or Sage.
- The ability to organise and prioritise your own workload and meet deadlines.
- Good communication skills and the confidence to liaise with colleagues, customers, and suppliers.
- A proactive approach, with the ability to identify issues and take action to resolve them.
- The ability to work independently while also being a supportive member of a small finance team.

Qualifications

A formal accountancy qualification is not essential.

We would welcome applications from candidates who are:
- AAT qualified or part-qualified;
- Studying towards an accountancy qualification;
- Qualified or part-qualified in another recognised accountancy qualification; or
- Experienced bookkeepers with strong practical accounting experience.

Relevant experience will be considered alongside formal qualifications.

What We Offer

This is a varied role within a growing privately owned Group, providing the opportunity to develop your accounting knowledge and take on additional responsibility over time.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to work across a range of finance activities and Group companies, gaining exposure to areas including management reporting, cash flow, financial analysis, credit control, and finance process improvement.

Job Type: Full-time, Permanent

Salary: £30,000-£35,000 depending on experience and qualifications

Reporting to: Financial Controller

company: Oasis Business Personnel Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Job Purpose:

We are seeking an organised and detail-oriented Payroll & HR Administrator to join a multi-site, multi-entity Group based in Daventry.

The successful candidate will prepare the month-end payroll for all entities within the Group and act as the main operational contact for the outsourced payroll provider. Working closely with the HR Administrator and the Finance department, you will ensure payroll inputs are accurate, fully checked and submitted within strict monthly deadlines.

This role would suit an experienced payroll or HR administrator with hands-on HR software experience, who enjoys detailed data checking and supporting employees with their queries. The position offers hybrid working, with one day working from home.

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

Payroll & HR Administration
- Act as the main internal contact and administrator for the Group payroll, liaising with the outsourced payroll provider.
- Gather, verify and consolidate all monthly payroll input variations, including new starters, leavers, salary changes, bank updates, overtime, sickness, rotas, visa restrictions, holidays and unpaid leave.
- Extract and cross-reference time, attendance, overtime, holiday and absence records in BrightHR, working alongside the HR Administrator to ensure all data is correct.
- Review shift rotas, timesheets and overtime submissions in BrightHR to ensure manager approvals are complete prior to payroll submission.
- Check regularly that sickness, annual leave, parental leave, holiday and overtime records in BrightHR are correct, confirming with the nominated staff member for each site.
- Submit complete, audited payroll data files to the outsourced provider within strict monthly cut-off deadlines, once approved by the Finance department.
- Carry out initial checks on draft payroll reports, gross-to-net summaries and payslips returned by the payroll provider to confirm accuracy before sign-off.
- Run monthly HR reports and data extracts, including headcount, absence tracking and payroll variance summaries, using BrightHR.

Employee Queries & Compliance
- Act as the first point of contact for staff regarding payroll queries.
- Maintain strict confidentiality and full GDPR compliance for all sensitive employee and salary data.

Person Specification:
- Excellent attention to detail, with strong data-checking skills to identify discrepancies before payroll files are submitted.
- Highly organised with strong time management skills and the ability to manage monthly workflows.
- Able to work under pressure and consistently meet strict payroll deadlines.
- Clear communicator with a customer-service approach to resolving employee queries.
- Professional and discreet when handling confidential employee and salary information.
- Able to work collaboratively with HR, Finance and site-based colleagues.

Experience:
- Previous experience compiling and preparing payroll inputs for an outsourced payroll provider or external payroll company is essential.
- Good practical understanding of general payroll.
- Hands-on experience using HR software to track staff records, attendance and absence, and to generate data reports.
- Solid working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, including VLOOKUPs, basic formulas and data filters, for data preparation.
- Experience using BrightHR would be advantageous.

Hours of Work:
- Monday - Friday

Work Location:
- Hybrid (4 days in person / 1 day WFH)

Benefits:
- 20 days holiday plus public holidays.
- Hybrid working with one day working from home.
- Professional development and training opportunities.
- Supportive and collaborative working environment.
- Opportunities to contribute to process improvements and organisational growth.
- Employee benefits in line with company policy

title: Payroll Co-ordinator
company: Macildowie Recruitment and Retention - Agency - Permanent
description:
Payroll Co-ordinator - Permanent

Further information is available upon application, prior to interview.

The Opportunity

We are recruiting for an experienced Payroll Co-ordinator to join an established and busy payroll function within a growing organisation.

This is a hands-on payroll position, with responsibility for supporting the accurate and timely processing of multiple monthly payrolls, alongside associated expenses, payroll administration and employee benefits.

Working as part of a wider HR function, you will play an important role in maintaining accurate employee and payroll records, ensuring deadlines are consistently met and providing support with payroll-related queries.

The ideal candidate will have at 2-3 years' experience working within a payroll environment, be confident working with payroll systems and have a strong understanding of payroll processes, legislation and data accuracy.

Key Responsibilities
- Assist with the accurate and timely processing of monthly payroll runs, ensuring all information is checked and processed within strict deadlines.
- Support the processing of monthly expenses, ensuring accurate calculations and payments.
- Maintain and update employee payroll records, ensuring all information is accurate, complete and up to date.
- Carry out regular data entry, data cleansing and integrity checks across payroll systems.
- Respond to payroll-related queries from employees and internal colleagues, providing guidance and escalating more complex matters where necessary.
- Ensure payroll changes, adjustments and employee information are processed accurately and within agreed timescales.
- Prepare and process payroll costing information for the Finance team.
- Support the administration of employee benefits.
- Assist with annual salary review calculations, checking information and ensuring changes are accurately reflected.
- Work closely with colleagues across Finance, Payroll & HR to identify and resolve discrepancies, improve processes and maintain accurate records.
- Ensure all payroll activities are carried out in line with relevant legislation, GDPR and internal data protection requirements.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for someone with a solid background in payroll who can confidently support a busy payroll operation and take responsibility for ensuring work is completed accurately and on time.

You will ideally demonstrate:
- A 2-3 years' of experience working within a payroll environment.
- A good understanding of end-to-end payroll processes and associated administration.
- Knowledge of payroll legislation, including PAYE, National Insurance and pension contributions.
- Experience using payroll systems.
- Strong Excel and spreadsheet skills.
- Experience handling payroll queries and communicating with employees and internal stakeholders.
- A good understanding of confidentiality, GDPR and the importance of handling sensitive payroll information.
- Excellent attention to detail, accuracy and organisation.

Experience & Qualifications
- A recognised payroll qualification, although not essential.
- Experience handling employee benefits.
- Strong knowledge of Excel functions, including pivot tables.
- Experience supporting annual salary reviews and payroll costing exercises.
- Previous experience working with larger or multi-site payroll operations.

Personal Attributes

The successful candidate will be:
- Confident and proactive: Someone who is comfortable taking ownership of their responsibilities and managing expectations.
- Highly organised: Able to prioritise workloads and work to multiple payroll deadlines.
- Accurate and methodical: Takes pride in getting things right and spotting discrepancies.
- Strong-minded: Confident enough to challenge information, raise issues and ensure deadlines are maintained.
- A good communicator: Comfortable dealing with payroll queries and working with colleagues across different departments.
- A team player: Willing to support the wider team and contribute towards improving processes.

This is an opportunity for an experienced Payroll Co-ordinator/Administrator who enjoys the detail and responsibility that comes with payroll processing.

Someone who can hit the ground running, has a good understanding of payroll fundamentals and is confident working within a deadline-driven environment.

You don't necessarily need to hold a formal payroll qualification, but you must have solid practical payroll experience, a good understanding of payroll legislation and the confidence to manage your workload independently.

title: Temporary Purchase Ledger Clerk
description:
Temporary Purchase Ledger Clerk - Northampton

Location: Northampton
Contract: Temporary

We are currently recruiting for an experienced Purchase Ledger Clerk to join a well-established business based in the Northampton area on a temporary basis.

This is a fantastic opportunity for a proactive and detail-oriented individual who enjoys working in a busy finance environment and can hit the ground running.

Key Responsibilities:
- Accurately process and reconcile purchase ledger transactions.
- Code, match and process both stock and non-stock supplier invoices.
- Complete monthly supplier statement reconciliations.
- Carry out weekly stock reconciliations, ensuring deadlines are met.
- Maintain strong financial controls across payment processes.
- Investigate and resolve supplier and internal queries efficiently.
- Support month-end close activities and wider finance team requirements.

About You:
- A minimum of 2 years' experience within a Purchase Ledger or Accounts Payable role.
- Intermediate to advanced Excel skills.
- A good understanding of financial controls and fraud prevention.
- Strong attention to detail and excellent organisational skills.
- Confident communicating with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- A proactive, self-motivated approach with the ability to manage competing priorities.
- A collaborative team player with a professional and approachable manner.

What's on Offer?

An opportunity to join an established finance team, gain valuable experience and make an immediate contribution within a busy transactional finance function.

If you're available at short notice and looking for your next temporary opportunity in the Northampton area, we'd love to hear from you!
